title: Idempotent Stream Replay and Client-side Contract PRD (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
We need a developer-friendly, observable, and safe pattern for clients to resume or replay streaming Hosted API responses and tool-calls without causing duplicate side-effects or confusing developers. This doc proposes an idempotent stream replay contract and SDK ergonomics that cover: streaming text/structured frames, tool call boundaries, partial/structured output validation, and safe retry semantics for mobile and intermittent networks.

Background / problem statement:
- Mobile and flaky-network clients commonly drop streaming connections mid-response and need a way to resume rather than restart.
- Network-level retries or client replay can cause duplicate tool invocations (webhooks, database writes) when the model decides to call a tool mid-stream.
- Current streaming flows provide partial frames but lack a standardized resume token and deterministic replay behavior. SDKs must pick either naive retry (dangerous) or complex manual dedupe (burdensome).
- Teams building production integrations with tool-calls need guarantees and telemetry to reason about duplicates and cost.

Goals:
- Provide a simple protocol for resumable streams: checkpoints, resume_tokens, sequence numbers, and idempotency tokens.
- Define safe tool-call semantics that allow eventual exactly-once or clearly-at-most-once behavior with observable markers.
- Surface SDK primitives that are ergonomic for web and mobile clients (auto-resume, backpressure, cost estimates).
- Add tracing/telemetry hooks that let infra and customers understand replays and duplicate attempts.

Non-goals:
- We are not providing hard distributed transactional guarantees across customer backends and Redwood-managed tools.
- Not addressing long-running background jobs orchestration; focus is interactive streams and short-lived tool calls.

High-level protocol sketch:
1) Stream start: client sends request_body + optional client_session_id + optional client_request_id (idempotency token). Server responds with stream_metadata frame: {server_stream_id, version, initial_checkpoint}.
2) Frames: each streamed frame includes: sequence_number (monotonic), frame_type (partial_text | structured_chunk | tool_call_start | tool_call_event | tool_call_end | checkpoint), payload, and cumulative_hash.
3) Checkpoints: server emits checkpoint frames at coarse-grained intervals (configurable by model/route). Checkpoint contains resume_token (opaque, signed by Redwood), last_seq, and a small schema snapshot (if structured output).
4) Resume flow: client reconnects with server_stream_id + resume_token. Server validates token and either: a) resumes from next_seq, streaming remaining frames; or b) rejects (stale) and provides a short summary with ``restart_hint``.
5) Idempotency for tool calls: when a tool_call_start frame is emitted, it includes tool_call_id (uuid), deterministic_call_signature (sha256 of inputs + model-version + logical nonce). If server detects a replay for a tool_call_id already observed, it will not re-invoke the tool and will instead stream a replayed tool_call_event with replayed=true and an invocation_reference (for observability).

Tool-call modes (developer configurable per route):
- at_most_once (default): server guarantees tool invocation will be attempted at most once per tool_call_id. Replays will replay previous result frames. This is safe but may drop an invocation if network prevented acknowledgement.
- best_effort: server may re-invoke on resume if previous call likely did not execute (higher risk of duplicates).
- transactional (enterprise): partner integrations that provide a webhook-confirmation handshake (customer-supplied ack) can enable stronger semantics; requires extra contract.

Structured output and schema negotiation:
- At session start, client may provide expected_schema (json-schema url or inline). Server includes a schema_snapshot in checkpoint frames.
- Partial validation: server emits structured_chunk frames that include validity: VALID | SOFT_ERROR | INVALID and a confidence score. Client SDK surfaces soft errors to UI but allows developer override.
- Schema evolution: schema_snapshot has version and compatibility_hint. Resume tokens can carry last_validated_schema_version to ensure clients and servers can reconcile.

SDK ergonomics (recommended primitives):
- StreamingSession object (JS/Swift/Kotlin): start(request, opts) -> returns {stream_id, events}. Options include auto_resume: boolean, resume_window_seconds: int, idempotency_token.
- subscribe(callbacks): onPartial(frame), onToolCallStart(meta), onToolCallResult(result), onCheckpoint(info), onResumeRejected(reason).
- retryPolicy: automatic resume attempts with exponential backoff, capped at resume_window_seconds. SDK keeps side-effect safety by default: if tool_call detected in-flight, SDK waits for explicit toolCallResult frames unless developer sets allow_client_retry=true.
- Developer hooks: onDuplicateToolCall(tool_call_id, invocation_reference) and allow providing custom dedupe handler that can call customer backend to check idempotency.
- Lightweight memory option for mobile: SDK can persist minimal resume metadata (stream_id, last_seq, resume_token) encrypted in platform keystore.

Observability and telemetry:
- Events emitted for tracing: stream_started, checkpoint_emitted, resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_reject, tool_call_invoke, tool_call_replay, duplicate_detected.
- Token-level cost_delta included in checkpoint frames to help mobile devs show remaining quota.
- Customer-facing logs: invocation_reference can be mapped to Redwood console for per-tool-call traces.

Rollout and backwards compatibility:
- Phase 1 (default rollouts): implement checkpoint + resume_token + basic resume flow for streaming text only; tool_call frames will be emitted but server will not yet implement automatic dedupe; SDK disabled by default.
- Phase 2 (safe tool-call idempotency): enable tool_call_id and server-side dedupe logic for at_most_once; SDK surfaces onDuplicate hooks.
- Phase 3 (schema snapshots + transactional webhooks): opt-in enterprise mode for transactional guarantees and webhook ack.

Failure modes and security considerations:
- Replay token leakage: resume_token must be short-lived (TTL) and signed; include audience and bounds. Recommend TTL default 10 minutes for public hosted API, configurable for Dedicated.
- Malicious replay: server must validate deterministic_call_signature and ignore arbitrary replay attempts that alter signatures.
- Privacy: partial frames and checkpoints must not leak internal tool output beyond configured routing; maintain data residency controls for Private deployments.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Server emits checkpoints with resume_token and sequence numbers for streaming text routes.
- Basic client library (JS) can resume streams using resume_token and receives remaining frames in-order.
- Tool_call frames present in stream with tool_call_id and deterministic_call_signature (no automatic dedupe yet).
- Telemetry events for resume_success/resume_reject appear in Redwood Console.

Success metrics:
- Reduce full-response re-requests by 60% for clients with transient disconnects (instrumented via telemetry).
- <1% of resumed sessions produce duplicate tool invocations in phase 2 (measured across partners integration tests).
- Developer satisfaction score improvement for SDK ergonomics (qual feedback).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Resume token TTL vs user experience: longer TTL easier for reconnects, higher security risk.
- At-most-once vs best-effort tradeoffs for developers relying on tool side-effects.
- How to propagate cost transparency to SDKs without leaking sensitive billing data.

Next steps / milestones:
- 2-week spike: implement resume_token signed format and implement sequence_number frames for streaming infra (eng-serving-runtime + infra).
- 4-week prototype: JS SDK auto-resume demo + Redwood console telemetry for resume events (devex + console team).
- 8-week internal beta: enable server-side dedupe for tool_call_id on a small set of tool integrations (solutions-engineering).

Appendix: example frames (informal)
- stream_metadata frame: {server_stream_id: "s-01X...", version: "v1", initial_checkpoint: {resume_token: "rtk..", last_seq: 0}}
- partial_text frame: {seq: 12, type: "partial_text", text: "...continued", cumulative_hash: "h3f2.."}
- checkpoint frame: {seq: 20, type: "checkpoint", resume_token: "rtk..", schema_snapshot: {version: "s1"}}
- tool_call_start: {seq: 21, type: "tool_call_start", tool: "email-send", tool_call_id: "uuid-123", deterministic_call_signature: "sha256:..", payload: {to: "x@org", subject: "..."}}
- tool_call_result (replay): {seq: 25, type: "tool_call_result", tool_call_id: "uuid-123", replayed: true, invocation_reference: "inv-99"} 

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus review on plumbing for resume_token lifecycle and SDK default safety model.
- Security and SRE: confirm limits for resume_token signing and replay rate-limiting.
- Solutions-eng/CS: think about partner onboarding checklist for identifying integrations that cannot tolerate duplicates.

Document owner: Aisha Patel (product-hosted-api).
